title: Victoria sponge
summary: Two buttery almond sponges sandwiched with a quick raspberry chia jam and softly whipped cream, dusted on top.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F). Grease two 20 cm (8 in) round pans and line the bases with parchment.
Simmer the raspberries and erythritol for 5 minutes, mashing them, then stir in the chia seeds and leave to thicken while you make the cake.
Beat the butter and erythritol for 3 minutes until light. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Whisk the almond flour, coconut flour, baking powder and salt together and fold them in, then fold in the almond milk to a soft dropping consistency.
Divide between the pans, level, and bake 20–25 minutes, until golden and springy. Cool 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack and cool completely; almond sponges are fragile while warm.
Whip the cream with 1 tbsp powdered erythritol to soft peaks.
Spread the jam over one sponge, then the cream, and set the second sponge on top. Dust with the remaining powdered erythritol.
dairy_free_notes: Dairy-free butter gives a slightly less rich crumb, and whipped coconut cream is softer, so fill the cake shortly before serving.
tips: For the classic jam-only version, leave out the cream and use a little more jam.

origin.history: The cake is named after Queen Victoria, who is said to have enjoyed sponge cake with her afternoon tea; the link to the queen herself is traditional rather than documented. Reliable baking powder from the mid-nineteenth century made a light, raised butter sponge practical, and a jam-filled sandwich of two such layers became a fixture of the English tea table.
